questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was an Ivy League University - the opportunity to study in a top university in the USA.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I cannot put a finger on the academic experience - the professors were super professional and engaged in their subject. Would have been nice with some more arrangements for foreign exchange students though. Also, be aware that american students are young when they attend college.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was somehow easy, but you have to seek up the information yourself. Just ask all the questions you have to the contact person - they are super helpful and have a great answer most of the times.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I arrived late and had to call the college security to let them know I was arrived. Then they came and drove me to my accommodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dartmouth places exchange students in dorm rooms - I had lived by myself.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You are automatically a part of the meal plan they provide.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The accommodation is not that great - keep that in mind!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to be aware that you are automatically given a dartmouth email account where you get the necessary information. Ask the contact person about how to find your login asap. You register for courses on DartHub and can also change your mind when you have arrived. I took skilessons during the winter term, but you have to register for this in december and the spots are limited and very popular. It is a way to learn skiing and also it is very cheap.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Your contact person, but you have to be active yourself.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be proactive and start the proces asap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Top notch professors!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It is undergraduate level and therefore not that challenging for a MA student. But, I still learned some new things.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is different. They have attendance and midterms which counts towards the finale grade - this is actually a good thing, because you do not have to worry about failing classes and can focus on your learning experience.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON20: Econometrics
ECON36: Theory of Finance
ECON62: Topics in Macroeconomics (Seminar)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of these courses were great!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None, ypu get vaccinations through your insurance. Do not take these vaccination at DK

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The whole stay is expensive. Be aware of this and do not expect to get every scholarship you apply for.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a lot of clubs - I took skilessons. You have to join something to socialize a bit.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of opportunities to join sport clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The skilessons were quite fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Skilessons again.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The first couple of weeks were difficult. But once you get into a rhytm it is alright.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Jpin some clubs and engage in study groups. The american students are very open to make new friends and socialize.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They really want to perform well.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Warm clothes in the winter (I experienced a day with -30 C)
- Some device to watch netflix on.
- Be prepared to that you might be the only exchange student from Europe, and therefore you have to be prepared to be open and ready to approach the local students. (They are super nice)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nah

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academics

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That you are left on your own to do almost everything and find out, what opportunities you have at Dartmouth.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I would recommend applying for another programme if possible - it would have been nice to have other students from the University of Copenhagen to spare with and share this experience with.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
